def-bounded-bv-data-on-line:
## Definition

Let $u$ be an almost-everywhere equivalence class of measurable functions on
$\mathbb R$ with $u\in L^\infty(\mathbb R)\cap L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R)$,
using the quotient convention of
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], the essentially bounded
class of [[def-l-infinity-on-a-measure-space]], and the local integrability
convention of [[def-locally-integrable-function-on-r-n]]. For $h>0$ define
$$D_hu(x):=u(x+h)-u(x),\qquad \operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{tr}}(u):=\sup_{h>0}\frac1h\int_{\mathbb R}|D_hu(x)|\,dx,$$
where the integral may be $+\infty$. The **bounded BV class on the line**
$\mathrm{BV}_b(\mathbb R)$ consists of those classes for which
$\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{tr}}(u)<\infty$; we write
$\operatorname{TV}(u):=\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{tr}}(u)$.

This translation-variation convention is the standard one-dimensional BV
seminorm on bounded locally integrable classes. It is unchanged by modifying
$u$ on a null set, because each translate of a null set is null. It does not
require $u\in L^1(\mathbb R)$: every bounded constant function belongs to
$\mathrm{BV}_b(\mathbb R)$ and has variation $0$.
def-piecewise-linear-fv-time-interpolant:
## Definition

Let $U_j^n$ be the states on a mesh from
[[def-monotone-finite-volume-entropy-scheme]], with cell-time slabs
$I_j\times[t_n,t_{n+1})$ and $t_n=n\tau$. The **piecewise-linear time
interpolant** $W_{h,\tau}$ is constant in $x$ on each cell and, for
$t\in[t_n,t_{n+1})$, is
$$W_{h,\tau}(x,t):=(1-\theta)U_j^n+\theta U_j^{n+1},\qquad \theta:=\frac{t-t_n}{\tau},\qquad x\in I_j.$$
The piecewise-constant state $\mathcal U_{h,\tau}$ and face flux
$\mathcal Q_{h,\tau}$ use the convention of
[[def-finite-volume-space-time-reconstruction]]. Values on mesh boundaries
are irrelevant to the corresponding Lebesgue classes.

The interpolant is affine in time on each slab and has the scheme values at
both time endpoints. Its purpose here is to obtain time-uniform local compactness
and the strong initial trace; the weak-limit supplier is applied to
$\mathcal U_{h,\tau}$ after proving that the two reconstructions have the same
strong local limit.
lem-monotone-fv-update-preserves-range-a:
## Statement

Let $u_0\in\mathrm{BV}_b(\mathbb R)$ and put $V:=\operatorname{TV}(u_0)$.
Let $U^n=(U_j^n)_{j\in\mathbb Z}$ be generated by
[[def-monotone-finite-volume-entropy-scheme]] under its full invariant-interval
CFL bound. Define the update map
$$H(a,b,c):=b-\lambda\bigl(F(b,c)-F(a,b)\bigr).$$
Then $H$ is nondecreasing in each coordinate on $I^3$ and $H(s,s,s)=s$ for
$s\in I$. Consequently,
$$a_-\le U_j^n\le a_+\quad(j\in\mathbb Z,\ n\ge0),\qquad \sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}|U_{j+1}^n-U_j^n|\le V\quad(n\ge0).$$
Moreover, for every $n\ge0$,
$$\frac h\tau\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}|U_j^{n+1}-U_j^n|\le (L_1+L_2)V.$$
For a sequence $x=(x_j)_{j\in\mathbb Z}$, the notation
$\|x\|_1:=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}|x_j|$ is used only when this sum is finite;
$x\vee y$ and $x\wedge y$ mean the coordinatewise maximum and minimum.
lem-monotone-fv-discrete-kruzhkov-inequa:
## Statement

Let $U^n$ be a scheme from
[[def-monotone-finite-volume-entropy-scheme]], satisfying the full
invariant-interval CFL bound. For $k\in\mathbb R$ define
$$G_k(a,b):=F(a\vee k,b\vee k)-F(a\wedge k,b\wedge k),\qquad q_k(s):=\operatorname{sgn}(s-k)(f(s)-f(k)),$$
where $q_k$ is the Kruzhkov entropy flux of
[[def-kruzhkov-entropy-solution]]. Then $G_k(s,s)=q_k(s)$ for every $s\in I$,
and for every $j\in\mathbb Z$, $n\ge0$ and $k\in\mathbb R$,
$$|U_j^{n+1}-k|-|U_j^n-k|+\lambda\bigl(G_k(U_j^n,U_{j+1}^n)-G_k(U_{j-1}^n,U_j^n)\bigr)\le0.$$
lem-monotone-fv-local-compactness-and-tr:
## Statement

Let $u_0\in\mathrm{BV}_b(\mathbb R)$ with $V=\operatorname{TV}(u_0)$ and
$I=[a_-,a_+]$. Let $(h_m,\tau_m)$ satisfy $h_m,\tau_m\to0$ and the full
invariant-interval CFL bound for the scheme of
[[def-monotone-finite-volume-entropy-scheme]]. Let $W_m$ and $\mathcal U_m$ be
the piecewise-linear and piecewise-constant reconstructions of
[[def-piecewise-linear-fv-time-interpolant]]. Then every subsequence has a
further subsequence for which $W_m$ converges uniformly in time in
$L^1(K)$ on every bounded interval $K\subset\mathbb R$ to a map
$t\mapsto u(t)\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R)$, continuous in local $L^1$,
with $u(0)=u_0$ and $a_-\le u(t)\le a_+$ almost everywhere. On that subsequence
the piecewise-constant reconstructions converge strongly to the same $u$ in
$L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R\times(0,T))$.
thm-monotone-finite-volume-entropy-conve:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $T>0$,
$f\in C^1(\mathbb R)$, and $u_0\in\mathrm{BV}_b(\mathbb R)$ in the sense of
[[def-bounded-bv-data-on-line]]. Put
$I=[\operatorname*{ess\,inf}u_0,\operatorname*{ess\,sup}u_0]$. Let
$F\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be locally Lipschitz, consistent with $f$,
nondecreasing in its first coordinate and nonincreasing in its second on
$I^2$, with coordinate Lipschitz bounds $L_1,L_2$ as in
[[def-monotone-finite-volume-entropy-scheme]]. For a family of meshes
$(h_m,\tau_m)$ assume
$$h_m,\tau_m\to0,\qquad \frac{\tau_m}{h_m}(L_1+L_2)\le1,\qquad \frac{\tau_m}{h_m}\ge c_*>0.$$
For each mesh, initialize by cell averages and update with the shared flux $F$.
Let $W_m$ be the piecewise-linear time interpolant and $\mathcal U_m$ the
piecewise-constant state reconstruction. If $u_0\in L^1(\mathbb R)$, assume
Dependent Choice $\mathrm{DC}$ in addition to $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; no DC
assumption is made when $u_0\notin L^1(\mathbb R)$.

Then there is a unique bounded Kruzhkov entropy solution $u$ on
$\mathbb R\times(0,T)$ with initial datum $u_0$, and
$$W_m\longrightarrow u\quad\text{in }C([0,T];L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R)),\qquad \mathcal U_m\longrightarrow u\quad\text{strongly in }L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R\times(0,T)).$$
For nonintegrable bounded BV data, existence is obtained from the local
finite-volume limit in the proof before local contraction gives uniqueness.
The theorem claims local convergence; global $L^1$ convergence requires
additional uniform tail control. The time-to-space lower bound $c_*$ is retained
from the approved convergence interface, and no system-valued or non-BV
entropy-process conclusion is asserted.
